about.title: Burlingame Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Burlingame's mix of local streets and heavy through-traffic on US-101, California Drive, and El Camino Real (SR-82) means collisions happen even in a city this size. San Mateo County's most recent data shows 104 injury collisions and 140 people hurt in a single year, with Thursday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. seeing a noticeable jump in reports. Whether your crash happened at a Burlingame Avenue intersection or on the freeway approach, the days right after matter: insurers move fast, and evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, or witness memory fades quickly. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect people hurt in Burlingame car accidents with an independent attorney who can review the details, handle communication with insurance adjusters, and explain your options under California law. There's no fee to get connected, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning you owe nothing unless they recover for you.

items.title: California's Filing Clock Is Shorter Than You Think
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. An attorney can help identify which deadline applies to your situation early on.

items.title: Comparative Fault Won't Automatically Sink Your Claim
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, so even if you're found partly responsible for a collision on SR-82 or California Drive, you may still recover a reduced amount. An independent attorney can help present the facts in a way that protects your share of any recovery.

items.title: No Recorded Statement, No Upfront Cost
items.desc: You're not required to give the other driver's insurer a recorded statement, and doing so without guidance can hurt your claim. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you.

items.question: I was hurt in a crash near the US-101 and Broadway interchange — what should I do first?
items.answer: Get medical attention even if you feel fine, since some injuries like whiplash or concussions surface later. Try to document the scene with photos and get contact information for any witnesses if you're able. Avoid giving a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company until you've spoken with an attorney, since early statements can be used to minimize your claim.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a Burlingame car accident?
items.answer: In most California car accident cases, you have two years from the date of the crash to file a lawsuit. That timeline can be much shorter, sometimes six months, if a government entity, such as a city vehicle or a defect on a public road, was involved. Because these deadlines vary by circumstance, it's worth having an attorney review your specific situation soon after the crash.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No, LawProactive is a free service and not a law firm itself. We simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who can evaluate your case. Those attorneys work on contingency, meaning they only get paid if they recover compensation for you.
